- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially when history shows rising trends.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes in history, leading to over-forecasting in the immediate next period.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — forecasts tend to revert to lower levels after recent high peaks, even if true price continues upward.
- Forecast lag: model often underreacts to recent price drops, failing to anticipate sharp downward turns.
- When history includes a prolonged upward trend, model tends to overestimate future prices, especially in the first 5–10 days of forecast horizon.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days of forecast, leading to overly optimistic price trajectories.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the first 10 days of the 30-day horizon, especially when history shows strong upward momentum.
- Model fails to capture “rebound” patterns after sharp declines — often underestimates recovery speed or magnitude.
- When true price spikes occur after a long downtrend, model tends to underestimate the magnitude of the rebound.
- Model overcorrects after minor price corrections — forecasts jump back up too quickly, missing the true trend continuation.
